issues.title: Terminal triangular-solve entry uses unspecialized right-hand-side indices
issues.failure_explanation: The displayed equation is presented as the terminal specialization of e:yi1i2iN. At that terminal index, every inner sum is empty, so its numerator must be c_{n_1...n_N}; c_{i_1...i_N} leaves unrelated free indices and does not define the claimed terminal entry.
issues.overall_effect: The printed base step of the recursive uniqueness discussion is ill-indexed. The general recurrence and the later algorithm already contain the correct indexed computation, so no formal theorem is defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In e:yi1i2iNnormal, replace the numerator c_{i_1i_2...i_N} by c_{n_1n_2...n_N}. No change to the recurrence, uniqueness argument, or algorithm is needed.
issues.why_classification: The general recurrence in e:yi1i2iN uniquely determines its terminal specialization because all inner sums are empty there. The unrelated free indices are a transcriptional defect that an intended reader can correct directly without repairing any inference or construction.

issues.title: Displayed operation counts are aggregated with the wrong constant
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the three immediately displayed operation-count components aggregate to M(5S-N+1). Those displayed components algebraically support M(5S-N-1); the old claimed total differs from their sum by 2M. This finding concerns the aggregation identity itself, independently of any separate audit of the component counts.
issues.overall_effect: The reported exact lower-order constant in the aggregate count is internally inconsistent with the displayed addends. Its correction does not change the leading asymptotic order.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the sum of the three displayed operation-count components and replace M(5S-N+1) by M(5S-N-1), where M=n_1...n_N and S=sum_j n_j. Retain the stated leading asymptotic order.
issues.why_classification: The repair requires correcting a genuine arithmetic aggregation rather than merely interpreting malformed notation, so it exceeds a typo. It is nevertheless short and routine, changes only the exact lower-order constant, and leaves the method, all dependent claims, and the O(n^{N+1}) complexity unchanged.

issues.title: Reverse Schur-basis exponential identity conjugates the wrong matrix
issues.failure_explanation: From exp(tA_j)=U_j exp(tT_j) U_j^*, the reverse identity necessarily contains exp(tA_j). For example, with T_j=diag(1,2) and U_j swapping the two coordinates, U_j^*exp(tT_j)U_j swaps the two diagonal exponentials and is not exp(tT_j) when t is nonzero.
issues.overall_effect: Read literally, the converse identity does not justify the subsequent transformation to e:sylvesterNDG and e:G. The theorem theo:evolND is proved independently before this equation and is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the reverse identity by exp(tT_j)=U_j^* exp(tA_j) U_j. The subsequent transformations to e:sylvesterNDG and e:G then require no further mathematical change.
issues.why_classification: The first identity in the same display uniquely forces the corrected reverse identity by unitary conjugation, and the subsequent formulas are consistent with that reading. The repeated T_j inside the conjugation is therefore a copied-matrix transcription error, not a defect requiring a new argument.

issues.title: Standard matrix-product contraction is misindexed

failure_location.quote: if $\X$ were a standard matrix and we wanted to compute $\A\X$, we would perform the sum in the definition of $\A\X$ along the first dimension of $\X$, i.e., $[\A\X]_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{n_j} a_{ij}x_{jk}$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that standard multiplication satisfies [AX]_{ij}=sum_k a_{ij}x_{jk}. The old paper's own mode-product definition instead places the summation index in A's second slot and X's contracted slot, supporting sum_k a_{ik}x_{kj}. The old expression keeps a_{ij} constant in k and generally computes a different, sometimes dimensionally unavailable, quantity.
issues.overall_effect: The explanatory formula can misdirect an implementation of the reshape-permute construction, although the intended use of an ordinary matrix product remains clear and no formal result depends on the misprinted indices.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed standard matrix-product formula by [AX]_{ij}=sum_k a_{ik}x_{kj}, with the sum over the common dimension. Leave the reshape-permute construction unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Both the standard definition of matrix multiplication and the paper's mode-product definition uniquely force these contracted indices. The surrounding prose already says that the first dimension of X is contracted, so an intended reader can correct the misprinted subscripts directly; no proof or implementation construction must be redesigned.

issues.title: Column-major dependency stride uses the wrong factor

failure_location.quote: the entry $y_{i_1i_2\ldots i_{j-1}k i_{j+1}\ldots i_N}$ occupies the position $index + (k - i_j)n_1n_2\ldots i_{N-1}$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \verb|cumprodN| stores the quantities $\{1, n_1, n_1n_2, \ldots, n_1n_2 \ldots n_{N-1}\}$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that changing the jth tensor index produces the offset (k-i_j)n_1n_2...i_{N-1}. Equation e:index establishes that the coefficient of i_j is the fixed product of dimension sizes n_1...n_{j-1}. The old offset both depends on an index value and ends at the wrong position, while the accompanying cumprodN(j) access expression uses the correct fixed stride.
issues.overall_effect: The printed offset formula is false and could cause access to the wrong dependency. The accompanying cumprodN(j) expression is consistent with e:index, so the separately described executable access rule is not defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated dependency offset by index+(k-i_j)n_1n_2...n_{j-1}, taking the product as 1 when j=1. Retain the accompanying access expression using cumprodN(j), which already implements this stride.
issues.why_classification: Equation e:index directly and uniquely gives the coefficient of the jth index as n_1...n_{j-1}, while the accompanying cumprodN(j) expression already uses that coefficient. The erroneous terminal factor is thus a transcriptional index error, and the executable access construction needs no mathematical repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: the entry $y_{i_1i_2\ldots i_{j-1}k i_{j+1}\ldots i_N}$ occupies the position $index + (k - i_j)n_1n_2\ldots n_{j-1}$

issues.title: Advertised advection–diffusion solution violates the stated initial data

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the solution of \eqref{e:uxt} is $u(\xx, t) = (1+\exp(t))\exp(-\xx\cdot\xx)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that (1+exp(t))exp(-x·x) is the solution of the full problem e:uxt. The old equation requires u(x,0)=exp(-x·x), but the claimed function has initial trace 2exp(-x·x). It satisfies the differential equation with that latter trace, while exp(-x·x) itself makes both the time derivative and the old right-hand side zero. Hence the literal old problem supports a different solution from the one advertised.
issues.overall_effect: The exact benchmark used to describe the advection–diffusion example is inconsistent with its old initial data. This does not affect theo:evolND or the general solver.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the initial condition in e:uxt to u(x,0)=2 exp(-x·x), and use that same initialization in the benchmark. This preserves the stated PDE and the advertised exact solution u(x,t)=(1+exp(t))exp(-x·x).
issues.why_classification: This one local normalization correction makes the full benchmark consistent while preserving its differential operator, nontrivial time-dependent exact solution, numerical purpose, and the general solver. No new proof is required and no affected theorem changes. It is not a typo because the old source also permits the coherent alternative of retaining the stated initial data and replacing the advertised solution by the stationary Gaussian, so the correction is not uniquely forced.
